scope: Endpoint-level joins for the 77 existing treatment assessments: 120 result records, 119 with reviewed endpoint/population/comparator/time/analysis scope and one source-limited initial-phase seizure result. Sixteen structured cellular observations distinguish experimental, tissue and clinical scope. Source-specific limitations and unverified denominators remain explicit. No universal allele-to-phenotype mapping, cell causality or treatment suitability is inferred.

endpointResults.endpoint: Multi-luminance mobility test at one year
endpointResults.population: 31 participants aged at least 3 years with biallelic RPE65 retinal dystrophy, sufficient viable retina and ability to perform the mobility test; 21 assigned treatment and 10 control.

Motor decline captures loss of walking/crawling but not every gait abnormality. Intraventricular delivery does not establish a particular cell subtype as the mediator.

endpointResults.label: Muscle weakness
endpointResults.population: 108 adults aged 23–78 years with SOD1-ALS randomized 72 to tofersen and 36 to placebo; the prespecified primary faster-progression population included 39 and 21 respectively.

Clinical function, circulating NfL and cell distribution/target engagement are separate observations; none demonstrates that the mapped cell subtype mediated this clinical trend.

endpointResults.label: Chorea
endpointResults.endpoint: Composite UHDRS and Total Functional Capacity
endpointResults.population: 791 adults with manifest Huntington disease randomized to 120 mg intrathecal tominersen every 8 weeks, every 16 weeks, or placebo.
endpointResults.comparator: Randomized placebo control; dose arms evaluated separately.
endpointResults.timeFrame: Ad hoc week-69 analysis after early treatment termination; the planned primary time point was week 101.
endpointResults.analysis: Planned primary measures were cUHDRS or Total Functional Capacity. Early stopping changed the analysis window; cUHDRS findings cannot be relabeled as isolated chorea measurements.
